Stated Claim / Post Context:
Furious judge orders freeze after 400 trees are cut down in East Potomac Park

The Trump administration says the tree removal has nothing to do with the president’s plan to renovate the park into a championship-level golf course.

Actual Article Body:
A furious federal judge ordered a freeze to the Trump administration’s plan for more than 500 trees to be cut down in D.C.’s East Potomac Park. More than 400 trees were cut down over the weekend.

Judge Ana Reyes raised her voice at government attorneys and said she was upset the government did not give proper notice before crews cut down the trees.

Stream NBC4 newscasts for free right here, right now.

“I trusted you all to not do precisely what you did,” she said.

Reyes said the government filed notice at 4:55 p.m. Friday saying up to 529 trees would be removed from the park, saying the trees needed to be removed in line with a rehabilitation plan from 2019.

News4 video on Saturday morning shows crews with chainsaws, and huge trees crashing to the ground. The government said about 400 trees were removed.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump announced plans to renovate the park’s golf course. Community members were outraged, and the D.C. Preservation League filed a lawsuit. The judge ordered the Trump administration to give reasonable notice before removing more than 10 trees or closing the golf course.

Reyes called an emergency hearing via video call on the holiday and ordered the National Park Service superintendent to testify under oath about why the work was done.

Washington, D.C., Maryland and Virginia local news, events and information

“I am thoroughly unamused right now,” she said. “I do not know how I could’ve made it any clearer that I did not want what was to happen to happen.”

“What has happened has caused the government to lose all credibility in this case,” Reyes went on to say.

The Park Service superintendent and government attorneys indicated that discussions and plans for the tree work in the park were first discussed earlier in the week. The judge wanted to know why the government didn’t let anyone know any sooner.

The judge issued an order stopping all work on the golf course until 7 a.m. Tuesday.

“If that order is violated by so much as two seconds, there will be contempt proceedings,” she said.

It was noisy for golfers at East Potomac Park on Saturday. The hum of saws filled the air as crews removed trees near the golf course.

The work grabbed the attention of people who use the park regularly.

“It's a sad sight to see. Very sad,” said John, a D.C. resident.

In June, Trump announced plans to transform the golf course at the park into a championship-level course.

The Park Service's Friday night filing states the trees “do not contribute to the historic landscape” of the park and are being removed as part of a “tree management and cultural landscape rehabilitation project.”

“With something that was submitted late yesterday, work begins today. We're anxious about the process,” said Kalli Krumpos, the advocacy director for the Washington Area Bicyclists Association.

The association has held three protests about this before, including one just last week.

“We think there needs to be public involvement. We want transparency. We want accountability,” Krumpos said.

News4 reached out to the D.C. Preservation League. The director said in a statement that the Trump administration is citing a 2019 cultural landscape report to justify the tree removal.

The statement goes on to say, “The government has promised the Court it will pursue all legally required approvals before proceeding with work on the site; this action directly violates those promises.”

The Washington Area Bicyclist Association is planning its fourth protest on Oct. 31.

News4 reached out to the Department of the Interior. A spokesperson emailed back to reiterate that the tree removal is part of that 2019 rehabilitation plan, saying, “The work will help restore the course's historic character and reopen views toward landmarks, including the Washington Monument.”

By Alex Griffing,

(AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes raged at a Trump Justice Department lawyer on Monday after the Interior Department cut down trees at East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C., without notifying the court, as she had previously ordered.

Judge Reyes reportedly screamed at the Trump lawyers and ordered a temporary stop to any further tree chopping at the park’s public golf course, which Trump is reportedly eyeing turning into a championship-style course.

Politico’s Kyle Cheney reported on the court proceedings, audio of which is not allowed to be shared publicly.

“Judge Reyes is furious,” Cheney wrote on social media, adding:

She has repeatedly told the government to inform her before any major demolition work was done on the golf course. The abrupt removal of 500 trees, without notice, “has cost the government all of its credibility” in this case.

REYES is yelling now. “Ignorance is not an excuse” she tells DOJ after they say they weren’t aware of the details of the tree-cutting plan, despite having an inkling.

“I was hearing from everybody on plaintiffs’ side that this was going to happen. I said repeatedly no, I trust the government,” Cheney quoted Judge Reyes as telling the court, adding, “I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done. Not only does that make it inexcusable … I am just at a total loss to understand what has happened here, other than — Occam’s razor time — that the government precisely intended to do precisely what it has done, which is intentionally delay letting the pantiffs and the court know what is happening so they can put a plan in place to clear hundreds and hundreds of trees.”

Conservationists, including the D.C. Preservation League and several golfers, are suing the Trump administration to stop the tree demolition at the park.

Independent journalist Scott MacFarlane also reported on the stunning back-and-forth between Judge Reyes and the Trump DOJ:

Judge to Trump Admin lawyer: “In what universe did anyone in your office think that was acceptable?!” Trump Admin: “We did our best…” Judge: “No you didn’t! You did your absolute worst!” Judge: “Beyond being upset and furious right now.. I’m just disappointed with the government”

MacFarlane added that Judge Reyes raised the prospect of contempt proceedings for the DOJ if any further trees were taken out without court approval:

Judge Ana Reyes reminds Trump Admin that there is an order halting any further work through at least 7am tomorrow.

“If that is violated by even two seconds….. there will be contempt proceedings”

–
